messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmefinancial.com>, Daniel Mendez <daniel.mendez@acmefinancial.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan for Acme Financial

Hi Priya / Daniel —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through the Redwood demo. Really appreciated the context on your fraud-detection use case and the requirements you called out around latency, token costs, and data isolation. As discussed, I put together an initial POC outline to align on success criteria, high-level timeline, ownership, and the minimal environment we need to evaluate model quality and performance.

Attached: acme_poc_plan_v1.pdf (POC outline) and acme_network_requirements.xlsx (network & access checklist).

High-level recap from today’s call:
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for real-time transaction risk scoring (90th percentile latency target <= 120ms per request under 100 RPS test) and maintain precision/recall within 5% of baseline model.
- Scope: 2 endpoints (score & explain), evaluation dataset: 10k recent transactions (anonymized), sample production workload pattern for batching simulation.
- Timeline: 4-week POC (kickoff + 2 weeks ingest & baseline + 1 week performance tuning + 1 week evaluation/hand-off).
- Success criteria (proposal):
  - Latency: 90th percentile <= 120ms at 20 RPS steady-state and acceptable degradation up to 100 RPS burst
  - Cost: token cost per 1k requests within X% of current spend (we’ll refine after access to baseline metrics)
  - Quality: end-to-end precision/recall drop <= 5% vs baseline model on agreed evaluation slice
  - Ops: automated rollout and fallback validated; logs/audits available for sample window

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm success criteria above (who owns sign-off?) — suggested: Priya (Business), Daniel (Engineering)
2) Agree schedule: propose kickoff Mon 30 Mar (2PM PT) — 30–45min intro + environment handoff
3) Provide access: secure SFTP for anonymized evaluation data + allow inbound connections from our staging IPs; security checklist attached for your security team to sign off.
4) Internal owners: Marissa (account lead), Dev Patel (integration & test harness), Sean Gallagher (performance tuning).

Priya — would you be able to confirm the success criteria owners and whether the kickoff time works? Once you confirm, we’ll update the POC doc and schedule the kickoff.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap and the POC doc. A couple of quick notes from our side after internal sync:

- Success criteria: The latency targets look reasonable, but we need a clearer definition for the evaluation slice (e.g., high-risk merchant cohort + time-of-day bucket). We also want to add "explainability" checks — sample explain responses must include top-3 contributing factors.
- Timeline: the week of 30 Mar is tight for sourcing anonymized data. Can we shift kickoff to Wed 1 Apr to give our data team two extra days?
- Security: our security team will review the network checklist; they asked for an architecture diagram showing where logs are stored (S3 vs. customer-controlled), as well as confirmation that no raw PII will be persisted in Redwood logs.

Also, small ask on owners: Priya (me) will sign off on business success criteria; Daniel will own engineering sign-off. Could you please list out the specific artifacts you need from us to start?

Thanks,
Priya

Hi Priya / Daniel —

Thanks — we incorporated your feedback into the POC doc. Two quick updates:

1) Kickoff moved to Wed 1 Apr at 2:00 PM PT (calendar invite sent). Please let me know if that conflicts.

2) Updated success criteria (short):
   - Evaluation slice: 10k anonymized transactions with a 20% high-risk merchant cohort and time-of-day buckets (UTC 00–06, 06–12, 12–18, 18–24).
   - Explainability: each explain response should list top-3 contributing factors (human-readable) — we will validate on a 500-sample set.
   - Latency: 90th percentile <= 120ms at 20 RPS steady-state; degradation profile acceptable up to 100 RPS burst.
   - Quality: precision/recall delta <= 5% vs baseline on evaluation slice.

What we need from Acme to start ingestion/tests:
- Anonymized CSV (or parquet) with the following columns: transaction_id, timestamp (ISO), merchant_id (hashed), amount, merchant_category, features_json (JSON string of model input features). Sample: 10k rows.
- SFTP credentials OR a pre-signed S3 link to a zip of the dataset. If SFTP, please whitelist our staging IPs: 34.83.12.45, 34.83.12.46.
- Confirmation from security that storing logs in our customer-controlled S3 bucket is acceptable OR confirmation of requirements if you want us to store logs in your environment. We will not persist raw PII in logs — only hashed/hashed identifiers and sampling metadata per our retention policy.

Attached: updated acme_poc_plan_v1.pdf (v1.1) and a short architecture slide for your security team.
